title: a callback whose callee's visible body invokes it is part of the pinned graph, and the route names the callee whose body ran it

xfail.reason: The fork accepts this program, grants the pin, and RUNS it. Measured 2026-08-23 through conformance/runner/backend-go.mjs: zero diagnostics, exit 0, stdout ["1"] — where the reference reports SMITHERS3001@16:1 with the route `... #pinned -> invoking-callee.mod.sm#run`. This is the fail-open direction and the program is otherwise legal, so nothing else in the compile reports it: `eval` is not refused on its own, only the pin refuses it, and the pin was granted. It is a MISSING WALK rather than a missing subsystem, and the evidence is that the fork owns every neighbouring piece: it charges `eval` in the pinned function's own body (`native pin failed: TypeScript is required through main.sm#scoped`), it charges it inside an immediately-invoked function expression, and it charges it inside a `Layer.provide` callback naming the anonymous hop (`... #scoped -> main.sm#<anonymous>`). What it does not do is ask which VALUE reaches a call whose selected signature is a parameter's function type — so a callback handed to an ordinary visible callee is never entered. 21-native-pin/a-class-instance-method-is-part-of-the-pinned-graph is the same missing question in its other spelling and fails the same way, while this case's own twin, a-callback-a-callee-only-stores-still-satisfies-the-pin, passes on the fork for the WRONG REASON: a backend that enters no callback at all satisfies the negative half of the pair automatically, which is exactly why the pair must be read together and why the negative alone certifies nothing.
xfail.doc: specification/requirements.mdx, 'Inference' (Locked): 'Requirement inference MUST be transitive through ordinary calls.' specification/compatibility.mdx, 'Native Pin' (Locked): 'A native pin MUST be a checked assertion over the complete transitive graph. Compilation MUST fail if any reachable operation or provider requires TypeScript. The diagnostic SHOULD show the dependency path that introduced the requirement.' `run(() => eval(...))` reaches `eval` through an ordinary call, so the requirement is inferred and the assertion must fail.

notes: THIS CASE IS HALF OF A PAIR and is worth nothing alone: its twin 21-native-pin/a-callback-a-callee-only-stores-still-satisfies-the-pin is the identical program with `run` replaced by a callee that only returns its parameter, and that one must COMPILE AND RUN. Together they state the rule in the only form that is checkable — ENTER THE CALLEE'S VISIBLE BODY AND CHARGE WHAT THAT BODY INVOKES — and refuse the two plausible wrong rules: 'charge callback arguments' turns the twin red, and 'a callback is deferred' turns this one green. `eval` is the corpus's existing `TypeScript` contributor (18-typescript-requirement, and 21-native-pin/a-pin-reaching-typescript-is-rejected pin the classification independently), chosen here so that the only diagnostic in the program is the pin's: the route is then the entire content of the expectation, and the twin can be an `expect: "output"` case that really runs. `messageContains` pins the composed route because a pin refused with an EMPTY route satisfies a code-and-position expectation exactly; naming `invoking-callee.mod.sm#run` is what proves the refusal came from reading the callee's body rather than from a rule about the argument, and the callee lives in another module so the route has to name the module that DECLARES it.
